_comment: Framework-based extraction. Edit freely. 'requires' declares the minimum text needed — fields marked full-text stay blank for abstract-only sources rather than being guessed at. 'inferred: true' marks fields the reviewer constructs rather than reads off the page.
review: AI and generative AI in management, business, and accounting education

TCCM.citation: Paul, J. & Rosado-Serrano, A. (2019). International Marketing Review, 36(6), 830-858.
TCCM.purpose: Characterises a body of literature and surfaces gaps. Applies to essentially any study, empirical or not.

CIMO.citation: Denyer, D., Tranfield, D. & van Aken, J.E. (2008). Organization Studies, 29(3), 393-413.
CIMO.purpose: Builds design propositions of the form: in context C, intervention I invokes mechanism M to deliver outcome O. Presupposes that something was actually done — it does not fit perception or attitude studies with no intervention.

fields.name: theory_named
fields.prompt: Theoretical frameworks the paper explicitly names (TAM, UTAUT, TPB, constructivism, self-determination theory, etc.). 'None stated' is a legitimate and common answer — never infer a framework the paper does not name.

fields.name: theory_role
fields.prompt: How theory is used: testing an existing theory, extending one, building new theory, framing only (cited but not operationalised), or none.

fields.name: context_country
fields.prompt: Country or countries of the study. 'Multiple' if comparative, 'Not stated' if absent.

fields.name: context_discipline
fields.prompt: Disciplinary setting of the education studied.

fields.name: context_setting
fields.prompt: Delivery setting: face-to-face, online, blended, or not stated.

fields.name: characteristics_constructs
fields.prompt: The key variables or constructs the study examines (e.g. perceived usefulness, academic integrity, learning performance, self-efficacy). List them as the paper names them.

fields.name: characteristics_relationships
fields.prompt: Relationships the study proposes or tests between those constructs, including direction (e.g. 'perceived ease of use -> intention to adopt', 'AI use -> reduced critical thinking'). Note mediators and moderators where present.

fields.name: method_design
fields.prompt: Research design. Conceptual pieces and reviews are not empirical — label them as such rather than forcing an empirical category.

fields.name: method_sample
fields.prompt: Who or what was studied, and how many. Give the number in digits where stated.

fields.name: method_analysis
fields.prompt: Analytical technique (SEM, PLS-SEM, thematic analysis, ANOVA, regression, content analysis, etc.).

fields.name: cimo_applicable
fields.prompt: Does this study examine an actual intervention — something introduced, deployed, or trialled? Answer 'no' for perception, attitude, and opinion studies where AI was merely asked about, and for conceptual pieces. When 'no', leave the remaining CIMO fields blank; that pattern is itself a finding about the literature.

fields.name: cimo_intervention
fields.prompt: What was actually introduced or done: the AI system, how it was deployed, by whom, and over what period. Be specific — 'ChatGPT-4 used for formative feedback on weekly essays over one semester' rather than 'ChatGPT used'.

fields.name: cimo_mechanism
fields.prompt: The generative mechanism — why the intervention produces the outcome. Papers rarely state this outright; it is usually reasoned from the discussion section. Record the paper's own explanation where it gives one, and mark the row for review where you are reasoning beyond what is written.

fields.name: cimo_outcome
fields.prompt: Effects reported, including direction and whether they were intended. Record null and negative results as carefully as positive ones — those are the findings most often lost in synthesis.

fields.name: key_findings
fields.prompt: The paper's headline finding in one or two sentences, in its own terms. Not your assessment of it.

fields.name: limitations_stated
fields.prompt: Limitations the authors themselves acknowledge. Only what they state — not limitations you observe.
